title: Euclidean Geometry: Midpoint Theorem and Quadrilaterals
seo_title: Grade 10 Euclidean Geometry Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Revise basic results established in earlier grades; investigate, justify and apply the properties of special quadrilaterals (kite, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square and trapezium); investigate and prove the midpoint theorem and its converse.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 Euclidean geometry worksheets: midpoint theorem and properties of parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, kites and trapeziums. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Midpoint line = half the third side.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Midpoint theorem: the line joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half as long.
  • Parallelogram: opposite sides and angles are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other.
  • Rectangle: diagonals are equal. Rhombus: diagonals bisect at 90°. Square: both.
  • Kite: one diagonal bisects the other at 90°.

Examples

Example

D and E are midpoints of AB and AC; BC = 14 cm

DE ∥ BC

Answer: DE = 7 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
DoublingThe midpoint line is half the third side.
Equal diagonalsOnly in rectangles and squares.
Kite or rhombusA kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides.

items.q: D and E are midpoints. AB = 18. Find DE.
items.e: Triangle Midsegment Theorem: the midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long. DE = 18 ÷ 2 = 9.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 4x − 3 and CD = 5x − 10. Find AB.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: 4x − 3 = 5x − 10, so x = 7. AB = 25.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE = 4x − 2 and ED = 3x + 6. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so BE = ED: 4x − 2 = 3x + 6, so x = 8.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = 4x − 2 and EC = 3x + 2. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: 4x − 2 = 3x + 2, so x = 4. AC = 2 × 14 = 28.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.
items.e: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: x = 180 − 51 = 129.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = x + 1 and CD = 4x − 17. Find AB.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: x + 1 = 4x − 17, so 3x = 18 and x = 6. AB = 7.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.
items.e: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: x = 180 − 59 = 121.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent: x = 65.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE = x + 11 and ED = 6x − 14. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so BE = ED: x + 11 = 6x − 14, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE = 4x − 5 and ED = 5x − 17. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so BE = ED: 4x − 5 = 5x − 17, so x = 12.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE = 3x + 6 and ED = 6x − 3. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so BE = ED: 3x + 6 = 6x − 3, so 3x = 9 and x = 3.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.
items.e: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: x = 180 − 91 = 89.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = 6x − 4 and EC = 2x + 28. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: 6x − 4 = 2x + 28, so 4x = 32 and x = 8. AC = 2 × 44 = 88.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = x + 15 and EC = 6x − 30. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: x + 15 = 6x − 30, so 5x = 45 and x = 9. AC = 2 × 24 = 48.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. BE = 3x − 6 and ED = 4x − 13. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so BE = ED: 3x − 6 = 4x − 13, so x = 7.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = 4x + 8 and EC = 6x + 4. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: 4x + 8 = 6x + 4, so 2x = 4 and x = 2. AC = 2 × 16 = 32.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.
items.e: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: x = 180 − 80 = 100.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus with diagonals meeting at E, and ∠ABE = 27°. Find ∠BAE.
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so ∠AEB = 90°. ∠BAE = 180 − 90 − 27 = 63°.

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 7. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 14 and ∠AEB = 90°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 5x + 7 and BD = x + 32. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: x + 32 = 2(5x + 7), x = 2.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 2x − 5 and BD = 6x − 28. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: 6x − 28 = 2(2x − 5), x = 9.

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 6. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 12 and ∠AEB = 90°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 2x + 2 and BD = 5x − 2. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: 5x − 2 = 2(2x + 2), x = 6.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus, and ∠BAC = 46°. Find ∠BAD.
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles, so ∠BAD = 2 × 46° = 92°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus, and ∠BAC = 41°. Find ∠BAD.
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles, so ∠BAD = 2 × 41° = 82°.

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 4. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 8 and ∠AEB = 90°.

items.q: A rhombus has one side of length 20. What is its perimeter?
items.e: All four sides of a rhombus are congruent: 4 × 20 = 80.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 3x − 5, CD = 4x − 12, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 3x − 5 = 4x − 12, so x = 7.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has perpendicular diagonals?
items.e: Rhombuses (including squares) and kites have perpendicular diagonals. Rhombus.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are congruent?
items.e: Rectangles (including squares) have congruent diagonals. A general rhombus does not. Rectangle.

items.q: Which property does a rectangle have that a general parallelogram does not?
items.e: Every parallelogram has the other three properties. Its diagonals are congruent.

items.q: Which fact is enough to prove ABCD is a parallelogram?
c: One pair of sides is parallel
items.e: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, it is a parallelogram. The diagonals bisect each other.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 2x + 9, CD = 4x − 1, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 2x + 9 = 4x − 1, so 2x = 10 and x = 5.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has two pairs of consecutive congruent sides but opposite sides that are not congruent?
items.e: That is the definition of a kite. Kite.

items.q: Is a rectangle a parallelogram?
c: Only if it is a square
items.e: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides. Yes, always.

items.q: For what value of x is ABCD a parallelogram, if AB = 4x − 2, CD = 5x − 12, and AB ∥ CD?
items.e: A pair of opposite sides that is parallel and congruent proves a parallelogram. Set AB = CD: 4x − 2 = 5x − 12, so x = 10.

items.q: Is every rhombus a square?
c: Only if it is a trapezium
items.e: A rhombus is a square only if it has right angles. No, only sometimes.

items.q: Find the length of the midsegment of the trapezium.
items.e: The midsegment of a trapezium is the average of the bases: (20 + 29) ÷ 2 = 24,5.

items.q: In isosceles trapezium ABCD, the bases are AB and CD, and ∠A = 65°. Find ∠B.
items.e: Base angles of an isosceles trapezium are congruent: ∠B = ∠A = 65°.

items.q: In isosceles trapezium ABCD, the bases are AB and CD, and ∠A = 62°. Find ∠D.
items.e: ∠A and ∠D are same-side interior angles between the parallel bases, so they are supplementary: 180 − 62 = 118°.

items.q: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. ∠A = 57° and ∠C = 111°. Find ∠B.
items.e: In a kite, the angles between the pairs of unequal sides (∠B and ∠D) are congruent. 2 × ∠B = 360 − 57 − 111 = 192, so ∠B = 96°.

items.q: Find the length of the midsegment of the trapezium.
items.e: The midsegment of a trapezium is the average of the bases: (4 + 11) ÷ 2 = 7,5.

items.q: Find the length of the midsegment of the trapezium.
items.e: The midsegment of a trapezium is the average of the bases: (12 + 20) ÷ 2 = 16.

items.q: In isosceles trapezium ABCD, the bases are AB and CD, and ∠A = 61°. Find ∠D.
items.e: ∠A and ∠D are same-side interior angles between the parallel bases, so they are supplementary: 180 − 61 = 119°.

items.q: In isosceles trapezium ABCD, the bases are AB and CD, and ∠A = 55°. Find ∠D.
items.e: ∠A and ∠D are same-side interior angles between the parallel bases, so they are supplementary: 180 − 55 = 125°.

items.q: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. ∠A = 73° and ∠C = 113°. Find ∠B.
items.e: In a kite, the angles between the pairs of unequal sides (∠B and ∠D) are congruent. 2 × ∠B = 360 − 73 − 113 = 174, so ∠B = 87°.

items.q: In isosceles trapezium ABCD, the bases are AB and CD, and ∠A = 60°. Find ∠D.
items.e: ∠A and ∠D are same-side interior angles between the parallel bases, so they are supplementary: 180 − 60 = 120°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 121°, 110° and 50°. What is the fourth angle?
In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 60°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 60° = 120°.

items.q: An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 66° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 66° = 114°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 81°. What is angle C?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal: 81°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 94°, 88° and 71°. What is the fourth angle?
In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 126°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 126° = 54°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 120°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 120° = 60°.

items.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to DC and angle A = 125°. What is angle D?
items.e: Angles A and D are co-interior between parallel lines, so they add to 180°: 55°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 83°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 83° = 97°.

The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 30 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 8 cm and 15 cm. Side = √(8² + 15²) = 17 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 18 cm and 24 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 9 cm and 12 cm. Side = √(9² + 12²) = 15 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 30 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 30 = 15 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 4x + 2 and MR = x + 11. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 4x + 2 = x + 11. So 3x = 9 and x = 3.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Side = √(5² + 12²) = 13 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Side = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 4x + 6 and BD = 38 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 4x + 6 = 38, so 4x = 32 and x = 8.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 5x + 3 and BD = 43 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 5x + 3 = 43, so 5x = 40 and x = 8.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 20 cm. How long is BE?

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 5x + 1 and BD = 16 cm. Find x.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 3x + 1 and BD = 28 cm. Find x.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 3x + 1 and BD = 13 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 3x + 1 = 13, so 3x = 12 and x = 4.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 4x + 1 and MR = x + 25. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 4x + 1 = x + 25. So 3x = 24 and x = 8.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 2x + 2 and MR = x + 10. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 2x + 2 = x + 10. So x = 8 and x = 8.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 2x + 8 and BD = 18 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 2x + 8 = 18, so 2x = 10 and x = 5.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 32 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 12 cm and 16 cm. Side = √(12² + 16²) = 20 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 2x + 2 and BD = 12 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 2x + 2 = 12, so 2x = 10 and x = 5.
